svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Inter, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Saksham IQ — the AI pipeline, end to end
What is a model, what is pure Python, and where the fence between them runs. Every box is a real module in this repository.
1 · THE DAY IS PLANNED — overnight, and no model touches it
planner_runner.sweep()
Runs itself every planner_interval_seconds and
freezes a plan for every child who has none for
today, so the agent's latency is never in front
of a waiting three-year-old. Idempotent: the
freeze is a unique constraint, not this code.
plan_service._candidates()
Exactly one level per subject — the first weak
one, else the first unfinished unlocked one —
and never two from the same subject. Every
subject is in every day: three stages for Play
Group, six for Nursery and UKG.
app/ai/planner — a LangGraph graph, all of it pure
gather
order
freeze
order = open on a level they will get right · the shaky ones early, never first · finish on a win
daily_plans + daily_plan_items
One frozen plan per child per day, and `source`
is always 'deterministic'. There was a model
here, fenced by a validator; the fence held and
it went anyway. The cursor is `completed_at`,
written by the award — never inferred.
2 · THE CLASS OPENS — the plan is a gate, not a suggestion
the web app opens on the class
`/` and `/home` send a signed-in
child straight to /ai-teacher. The
schedule strip rides above every
screen. The client renders a turn and
reports back; it decides nothing.
POST /playground/teacher
`/{child_id}/open`, then
`/sessions/{id}/answer` and `/ask`.
The route still says playground
because that is where this started;
nothing about it is a sandbox now.
service.open_session()
Snapshots today's plan into
playground_sessions.plan_topics and
resumes at the plan cursor, so a
child who stopped picks the rest up.
_class_intro is said once a sitting.
plan_service.may_open()
A topic opens if today's frozen plan
holds it, or the child has already
finished it. Everything else is
tomorrow's — including the level this
lesson has just unlocked.
status = day_complete
The last stage through ends
the day. The class will not
reopen until tomorrow's plan
exists, and a reload cannot
get past it: the server refuses.
3 · ONE TEACHING TURN — the only place in the whole system a language model is allowed
A · WHICH WAY TO TEACH IT — teaching_policy_service.decide()
candidates — the action space (app/policy/actions.py)
The nine strategies: TELL · SHOW · EXAMPLE · STORY · CONTRAST · DO_TOGETHER ·
SENSE_SWITCH · PREREQUISITE · PARK. Early mode keeps five of them.
eligibility.decide() — the fence, and it is a separate step
Removes what the app's own rules forbid: parking a child early, an explanation
already spent on this question, a strategy the age band excludes, a prerequisite
that does not exist, a story for a child near tears. It never returns nothing.
selector.choose() — epsilon-greedy, 0.08, over the survivors only
A Q-table keyed on mode|mastery|rung|spent — the child's identity is deliberately
not in it. The hand-written ladder is the prior and decays as visits arrive, so
day one reproduces today's behaviour. Exploration cannot reach a filtered action.
out: one strategy, and which arm chose it
ladder · shadow (the ladder teaches, the table's pick is written beside it) · rl.
A database that will not answer is a fallback to the ladder, never an error.
B · WHAT TO SAY — retrieval, the syllabus, and the agent
rag.search() — teacher_notes.md + the syllabus itself
Free HuggingFace MiniLM embeddings, cosine similarity, with a keyword fallback
that is not an afterthought. Fenced on class_id, or the nearest passage to
"letters" is a UKG one. The answer keys — correct_answer, accept, options —
are never indexed: a model holding the key is one that can give it away.
questions.pick() — the question was written for this class
On the steps where the child chooses (match, quiz) the question, its answer and
its choices come from the authored syllabus for the child's own class, and the
model writes only the explanation that leads into it. A topic's title is not a
question: "can you show me pre-writing strokes?" is a heading, not an ask.
app/playground/agent.py — a LangGraph graph
START → retrieve → choose → teach → END, with fallback when there is no model
or the answer comes back malformed. Only `teach` calls out, and it asks for two
things at once: the explanation in the chosen strategy, and one question on it.
The same nodes run the hint and the reveal — neither invents a question.
app/ai/llm/client.py
One provider-agnostic call, with a
circuit breaker in front of it.
Groq · openai/gpt-oss-120b, a 6s
timeout and no retries, over one
pooled connection — the handshake
per call was most of what "the AI
is slow" meant. Three failures in a
row and it fails fast for a minute.
the deterministic teacher
No key, a timeout, an HTTP error or
a malformed body raises
LLMUnavailable, and the child still
gets several sentences out of the
author's own passages, an everyday
example, a question and its options.
Failure here is normal and quiet —
every caller has an answer ready.
C · COMPOSE THE DIRECTIVE — everything downstream of this line is pure Python again
safe_text() filters the words · leak.classify() tells scaffolding and a partial clue apart from handing the answer over, and only an
outright leak sets answer_leak_vetoed — a teaching turn is judged on its directive frames alone, because naming the thing you are
teaching is the lesson · ensure_options() so a question that wants a tap always has something to tap · hint_options() is built here in
plain Python rather than asked for, so a hint can never arrive without the answer among its choices · examples.for_turn() picks two or
three of the author's own visual_items, never the answer beside it · visuals.from_concept() draws the picture from the level's title.
teaching_policy_service.commit() → policy_episodes
One row per teaching turn, and no reward in it. The question, the rung, how
many strategies were spent, mastery either side, which arm chose and what the
other arm would have chosen, the eligible set, and the leak verdict. That is
what makes a moved table explicable afterwards. It runs on the turn's own
session — a second one waits out SQLite's whole busy timeout, on every turn.
4 · THE CHILD'S SURFACE — spoken, tapped, traced, said back
the explanation is said, not printed
Three or four sentences for the ear, kept on
screen only as sr-only text. What the child
looks at is the picture, the question drawn
large, and the example strip. A paragraph of
English above a two-year-old's question is not
something they can read.
POST /speech/synthesize → edge-tts
Microsoft Edge's free hi-IN-SwaraNeural, through
the app's own backend. One voice reads both
scripts, which is what the narration needs:
English with Devanagari quoted inside it. No
model is involved — text in, audio out, and what
is said was decided upstream.
the child answers
tap · trace · voice, whichever the step's
`expects` asked for. There is exactly one
microphone on the screen. The auto-advance
timer stays — the child is too small to press a
button — but it may only start once the
narration has actually been heard.
child_speech_service
"tree" for three, "wed" for red,
"do nahi teen" — cleaned by lookup
in kid_phonetics.json. No LLM. It is
given the options on screen and
never the answer, so a poor
transcript cannot be nudged right.
5 · MARKING AND PROGRESS — pure Python, and the only path that pays a star
stage.judge() — the answer-key boundary
Marks in plain Python from the authored key, and from nothing
else. A tap is marked by which button it was, never by
word-matching its label: contains_answer both puts an option
on the screen and marks it, so the two cannot disagree and a
child cannot tap the server's own answer and be told they are
wrong. Speech and typing keep the generous word matching.
lesson.py — the shape of a question, and of a stage
explain → say_it → draw → match → quiz. Every question gets
three turns: it is asked; a wrong answer brings the hint — the
thing explained more deeply, ending in a clue and two or three
choices; a second wrong answer brings the answer, told and
explained. That third turn expects "ready", is never marked and
writes no attempt. Five settled questions are one stage.
history_service.record_attempt() → attempts
The one log everything downstream reads: mastery,
the weak-skill list the planner reorders on, the
conductor's own view of the child. A teaching loop
that graded an answer and kept the verdict to itself
would leave both reading a partial history. The echo
is taught and never marked — that is the hardware.
learning_service.award_topic_completion() — the end of a stage
The same deterministic scorer the conductor ends a lesson with, run on a score computed out of
that stage's own topic_correct / topic_answered, where a question the teacher had to answer for the
child counts as one that did not land. It marks the level done, pays the manifest's stars, unlocks
the next level, re-checks the certificate and moves the plan cursor. There is no score anywhere on
the child's screen: five dots for the five questions, and which level of the day. Progress, not a mark.
Adventure is a progress board, and nothing else
It shows what is finished, what today's plan holds, what is sleeping until its turn and what is still
locked. Nothing on it starts a lesson — not from a subject card, not from a level node, not from the
schedule strip — because a second entrance can open a level the day's plan has not reached, which is
the one thing the gate exists to prevent. There is one teaching loop on the web and it is the AI
Teacher; the conductor still serves the mobile app, and nothing in frontend/ mounts it.
6 · THE REWARD, PAID DAYS LATER — the reason this is not RLHF
retention_service.on_attempt()
Every marked answer passes through here.
It settles whatever probe this attempt
answers and schedules what it earns.
It runs on its own session, deliberately:
settling the fifth question of a stage
calls the award, which needs the write
lock the probe would otherwise hold.
schedule the day-2 probe
A correct answer schedules a probe two
days out and attaches every unpaid
episode for that skill to it. The teaching
turns that made this moment possible are
now waiting on one piece of evidence, and
it is not the answer the child has just
given in the same breath.
days later, the probe is an ordinary attempt
Two days on, the child meets that skill
again. That attempt is the probe: it
resolves, pays every attached episode,
and the table moves. A pass schedules the
day-7 one, which separates a strategy
that held for 48 hours from one that held
a week. A different form is transfer.
settle_probe() — paid once
Refuses a probe that already has a
resolved_at, and reaches back only
ATTRIBUTION_WINDOW days for the
episodes it pays, so June's retention
result cannot be credited to April's
teaching. Applying one probe's
evidence twice is not a rounding error.
the reward function — and it has exactly one source
+1.00 the retention probe passed −1.00 the probe failed
+0.35 transfer: the same skill in a different form −1.50 answer_leak_vetoed
A leak costs more than a passed probe pays. A strategy that reaches today's right answer by handing it
over produces a correct attempt today and a failed probe on Tuesday — which is the whole design.
the Q update
Q(s,a) ← Q(s,a) + α · ( r + γ · max Q(s′,a′) − Q(s,a) )
The successor is the pessimistic one — one rung higher, one strategy fewer — because a strategy that
works is not judged by the bootstrap term at all. It is judged by the probe that pays it days later.
The state is mode|mastery|rung|spent: what is learned is how to teach a kind of moment, not a child.
the moved table is what the selector reads on the next turn
7 · THE SWITCHES, AND THE HONEST VERDICT
rollout.py — who it may teach today
POLICY_MODE is shadow in production:
the hand-written ladder teaches, the
learned policy's choice is written beside
it, and nothing a child hears changes.
`on` + POLICY_ROLLOUT_FRACTION walks
stable hash — nobody flips mid-sitting.
health.py — the automatic kill switch
Consecutive failures of the learned path,
not a rate: one failed turn in a hundred
is a blip the fallback already handled
kindly; five in a row is an outage. Past
the threshold every child goes back to
the ladder for the cooldown. Nothing
here can stop a lesson.
POST /policy/disable · /enable
The manual switch, and it is an endpoint
so that turning the policy off needs no
deploy. That also made it reachable by
anybody, so outside development it wants
POLICY_ADMIN_TOKEN in an X-Policy-Token
header, and an unset token closes the
endpoint rather than opening it.
evaluate.py — replay, not a hunch
Ladder vs random vs Q-learning by
replay over the settled episodes:
where the candidate's choice matches
what was spent, the real reward
counts. No winner unless both arms
clear MIN_EPISODES and the gap
clears two standard errors.
THE ONE RULE THAT NEVER MOVES
No language model decides correctness, a score, a star, an unlock or a certificate. stage.judge marks in pure Python from the authored key; the branch decision is a pure
function; the planner has no model in it at all; and a reward is the retention probe's and nobody else's. "100% AI" means zero manual decisions on the child's surface — no
navigation, no menus, no "next" button — not that a model grades anything. A reward defined on "the child answered correctly" trains a teacher that hands the answer over.
